A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LexGen framework and dataset. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original dictionary-generation experiments, cross-domain and cross-lingual evaluations, routing ablations, and human evaluations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original in-domain and cross-lingual results, domain-generalization analysis, routing ablations, human evaluations, and appendix results.

M1.justification: The domain-specific/shared routing architecture, gating equations, layer placement, parameter sharing, and full-model fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. Additional model descriptions repeat existing Appendix A information.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three training domains, five unseen domains, six principal Indic languages, and Punjabi/Malayalam human evaluations. Although the full DDST comparison disappears, those unseen domains remain represented in the retained domain-generalization analysis.

E2.justification: V3 removes the entire DDST comparison against Base Transformer and NLLB reported in v2 Table 2. Its remaining DDST table reports only LexGen diagnostics, eliminating comparative evaluation for this generalization setting. Comparator membership in the retained IDST, IDDT, and human evaluations is unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported DDST evaluation loses the phrase-level ChrF++ comparison and retains the existing aligned-word P@1 and non-transliteration protocol. Retained training settings and metric parameters are unchanged. V3 labels the IDST table 'ChrF' despite retaining the ChrF++ specification in Section 4.3; this does not establish a changed computation.

E4.justification: Removing v2 Table 2 reduces evidence about comparative robustness across individual unseen domains. The overlap/non-overlap analysis, non-transliteration checks, routing-layer ablations, Gaussian-noise finding, and qualitative translation examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose single-run results in Appendix A; v3 repeats this information in Section 4.6. Neither adds seeds, uncertainty estimates, or a specified significance-testing procedure, and the existing statistical-significance claim remains.

E6.justification: V2 Table 2's five-domain, four-language results for NLLB, Base, and LexGen are absent from v3. Removed entries include broadcasting Hindi scores of 58.69 for Base versus 56.31 for LexGen, documenting a baseline advantage. All matched retained numerical tables, prompts, and translation examples are unchanged.

T1.justification: The routing and sigmoid-gating equations and their mathematical content remain unchanged. Removing the second equation number and adjusting notation do not introduce definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The core claims about domain-aware routing, a benchmark exceeding 75K translation pairs across six languages and eight domains, and generalization to unseen domains and languages remain. The broad baseline-superiority claim is also retained despite removal of the full DDST comparison.

C2.justification: V3 deletes v2 Section 5.2's interpretations connecting cross-domain performance to approximately 30% administrative/psychology overlap and NLLB's pretraining bias. Other mechanism explanations and the limitations concerning a single MNMT backbone and Indic-only coverage remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 adds a stated source-code and complete-dataset repository location, replacing the earlier sample-data access reference. Conversely, it omits the explicit 80%/10%/10% split description and DDST construction details specifying 500 examples per domain/language and translation followed by independent review. These are documentation changes, not established experimental changes.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to lexicon induction, translation models, and routing approaches remain the same. DictDis and NLLB reference changes update bibliographic information rather than introduce different works.

P1.justification: V3 reorders introductory and related-work passages, moves dataset-distribution discussion from Appendix B to Section 4.5, and consolidates DDST discussion. It also edits wording, author/affiliation information, and acknowledgements, while retaining most prose.

P2.justification: V3 removes the full DDST table, moves dataset statistics into the main text, and relocates Figure 1 nearer the method. The IDST table is enlarged and corrects bold highlighting for Base's administrative-Marathi and chemistry-Tamil wins. Other displays largely retain their structure.

improvement.justification: V3 adds code/data access information and improves some table presentation, but removes the main comparative evidence for unseen-domain performance, including baseline wins, while retaining broad superiority and generalization claims. Losing explicit split and DDST curation details further weakens transparency. These losses outweigh the limited documentation and presentation gains, although the method and remaining empirical evidence are intact.
